columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: WhatsApp Communities group multiple related groups under one umbrella.
WhatsApp Business and Business API support organizations communicating at scale.

strengths.title: Ubiquity and zero-friction onboarding
strengths.detail: Many members already use WhatsApp; joining is as simple as a link or admin invite.

strengths.title: Mobile-first and highly accessible
strengths.detail: Excellent mobile UX; lightweight and usable in low-bandwidth environments.

strengths.title: Group chats and Communities
strengths.detail: Group chats (hundreds of members), broadcast lists, and Communities for organizing multiple groups.

strengths.title: End-to-end encryption
strengths.detail: Chats and calls are E2E encrypted, supporting everyday privacy expectations.

weaknesses.title: Chat-only structure
weaknesses.detail: Primarily conversation, no threads, spaces, or rich community/course structures beyond chat.

weaknesses.title: Limited moderation and roles
weaknesses.detail: Basic admin controls (add/remove, group info); no robust role-based access or advanced community management.

weaknesses.title: No built-in monetization or membership tiers
weaknesses.detail: No native paid membership or tiered access, monetization must be external.

weaknesses.title: Notification overload and shallow archives
weaknesses.detail: High volume overwhelms members; finding past content is mostly search/scrolling, not structured discussion.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. WhatsApp is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

WhatsApp is a simple, secure, reliable messaging app available on phones around the world, wins on accessibility and zero-friction entry as a free conversation tool for communities of any size.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and WhatsApp side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On WhatsApp you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with WhatsApp

You can use both. WhatsApp keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on WhatsApp. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
